Full-color outdoor photograph, shot at eye level in clear afternoon sunlight, showing a red bicycle leaning against a white-painted brick wall. The bicycle stands left of center in a three-quarter side view, with its front wheel turned toward frame-left and the handlebars resting against the bricks. Its red steel frame has a curved top tube, black saddle, silver spokes, dark rubber tires, and a small metal bell on the right handlebar. The rear wheel sits close to the ground while the frame tilts back against the wall, casting a long angular shadow across the bricks. A narrow chain guard runs along the lower frame, and a few scuffs mark the red paint near the crank. In the foreground, pale concrete paving meets the base of the wall, scattered with several dry leaves and a thin strip of dust. Behind the bicycle, the white brickwork fills most of the background, its mortar joints forming an uneven grid; patches of sunlit brick are warm cream-white while recessed joints remain grey. Hard sunlight enters from the upper right, illuminating the bicycle’s right side and producing crisp shadows from the wheels, spokes, pedals, and handlebars across the wall. On the far right, the wall continues into open space with a bright patch of direct light and a darker band of shade near the pavement.
